public_rationale: OpenAI announced voice and image capabilities on September 25, 2023 [e5]. On May 13, 2024, it announced a rollout to free users of tools including web responses, data analysis, charts and file uploads [e6]. These announcements document functionality additions beyond model substitutions, but do not establish whether they materially changed practical usefulness for most users by October 2, 2024 [e5, e6]. The September 2025 usage study covers activity through July 2025; its reported aggregate findings do not supply the required launch-to-October-2024 comparison [e7].
limitations: Feature announcements do not measure representative adoption or practical benefit for most users [e5, e6].
The usage study reports conversation patterns, which do not by themselves establish user shares or changes in usefulness during the claim period [e7].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: ChatGPT, OpenAI's key revenue source, has not meaningfully changed since launch for most users.

statement.excerpt: OpenAI lives and dies on the revenue gained from ChatGPT, a product that hasn't meaningfully changed since it launched beyond adding new models that do, for most users, exactly the same thing.

from_speaker: hasn't meaningfully changed since it launched
for most users, exactly the same thing
our_interpretation: Assess the product-change proposition identified in the normalized claim; the revenue-dependence phrase supplies context.
The ordinary reading is that practical functionality and usefulness remained substantially unchanged for the majority of users between launch and publication.
New capabilities count as possible meaningful changes, but their existence alone does not establish their importance to most users.
Use the explicitly described launch-to-publication period.
criteria.support_condition: Representative evidence comparing launch with the product available by publication shows substantially unchanged practical functionality or usefulness for most users.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evidence shows that changes beyond model substitutions materially changed practical functionality or usefulness for most users by publication.

evidence.excerpt: We’ve trained a model called ChatGPT which interacts in a conversational way.
evidence.locator: Opening paragraph of the original announcement
evidence.explanation: This establishes the original conversational product baseline. It does not measure what most users subsequently valued.

evidence.excerpt: We are beginning to roll out new voice and image capabilities in ChatGPT.
evidence.explanation: This challenges the broad description of an unchanged product: users gained new input and interaction modes. It does not establish a material benefit for the majority.

evidence.excerpt: We are starting to roll out more intelligence and advanced tools to ChatGPT Free users over the coming weeks.
evidence.locator: Section 'Bringing more intelligence and advanced tools for free'
evidence.explanation: The accompanying list includes web responses, data analysis, charts, photo discussion and file uploads for free users. These are relevant functionality changes, but availability does not demonstrate their importance to most users.

evidence.excerpt: Using a privacy-preserving automated pipeline, we classify usage patterns within a representative sample of ChatGPT conversations.
evidence.explanation: This is relevant representative research, but its overall results extend through July 2025. They do not settle whether most users experienced material change by October 2024.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Representative evidence comparing practical functionality and usefulness at the November 30, 2022 launch and by October 2, 2024, showing whether changes beyond model substitutions materially affected most users.
